q: The highest point which shows the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest position is called a wave _____.
e: The highest point which shows the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest position is called a wave crest. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The lowest point which shows the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest position is called a wave _____.
e: The lowest point which shows the maximum displacement of a vibrating particle from its rest position is called a wave trough. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The distance between any two consecutive wave crests or two consecutive wave troughs is called _____.
e: The distance between any two consecutive wave crests or two consecutive wave troughs is called wavelength. Wavelength here means the distance from one crest to the next crest. Amplitude: the maximum displacement of the vibrating particle.

q: The SI unit of wavelength is the _____.
e: The SI unit of wavelength is the metre. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: Generally, the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of the same _____.
e: Generally, the wavelength is the distance between two nearest points of the same phase. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda. Amplitude: the maximum displacement of the vibrating particle.

q: The number of complete waves passing a point per second is called the _____ of the wave.
e: The number of complete waves passing a point per second is called the frequency of the wave. Frequency here means how many complete waves pass a point each second. Period: the time for one complete vibration.

q: The SI unit of frequency is the _____.
e: The SI unit of frequency is the hertz. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: One hertz is equal to one complete _____ per second.
e: One hertz is equal to one complete cycle per second. The physics in this sentence is built around cycle. Wavelength: the distance from one crest to the next crest.

q: The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests is called the _____ of a wave.
e: The time taken by the wave to travel the distance between any two consecutive wave crests is called the period of a wave. Period here means the time for one complete vibration. Frequency: how many complete waves pass a point each second.

q: The unit of period is the _____.
e: The unit of period is the second. The unit that belongs with this quantity is second.

q: The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the _____.
e: The period is the reciprocal or inverse of the frequency. Frequency here means how many complete waves pass a point each second. Wavelength: the distance from one crest to the next crest.

q: The mathematical relationship between period $T$ and frequency $f$ is _____.
e: The mathematical relationship between period $T$ and frequency $f$ is $T = \frac{1}{f}$. Frequency counts complete waves per second, and v equals f lambda.

q: The amplitude of a wave is the _____ value of displacement of a vibrating particle.
e: The amplitude of a wave is the maximum value of displacement of a vibrating particle. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The velocity of a wave is the _____ with which a wave crest travels.
e: The velocity of a wave is the speed with which a wave crest travels. Speed here means how fast the path length changes, with no direction. Acceleration: how quickly velocity changes.

q: The unit of wave velocity is _____.
e: The unit of wave velocity is $\text{m s}^{-1}$. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: Most of the periodic waves are represented by sine or cosine graphs, therefore they can be called _____ waves.
e: Most of the periodic waves are represented by sine or cosine graphs, therefore they can be called sine waves. Sine names most of the periodic waves are represented by sine or cosine graphs, therefore they can be called waves.

q: The relationship between the frequency, wavelength and velocity of a periodic wave is given by the equation _____.
e: The relationship between the frequency, wavelength and velocity of a periodic wave is given by the equation $v = f \lambda$. Wavelength is crest to next crest, and v equals f lambda.
